label: Doctor check-up

what_happens.title: What happens at a check-up
goals: The steps: waiting room, nurse, scale and height, doctor, listening, looking, goodbye
A check-up is how the doctor learns that a body is growing well
Every step is a look or a listen, and each one is short
what_happens.parentSkill: Name the steps in order and let your child tell you which one comes next.

who_is_there.title: Who is at the doctor
goals: A receptionist says hello, a nurse measures, the doctor checks
Their job is to help children stay healthy
The grown-up stays in the room the whole time
who_is_there.parentSkill: Talk about each helper by their job, and say that you stay in the room.

what_i_do.title: What I do at the check-up
goals: Stand tall on the scale, sit on the exam table, breathe in and out for the stethoscope
Open wide and say aah, keep still for a peek in the ears
Ask a question or say "wait please" any time
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise 'breathe in, breathe out' and 'say aah' with a toy stethoscope or a paper tube.

if_scared.title: If I feel worried
goals: The stethoscope can feel cold, the paper on the table crinkles, the light is bright
A cuff on the arm squeezes tight for a few seconds, then lets go
Calm tools: slow breaths, holding a hand, holding a toy
if_scared.parentSkill: Name the feeling and the plan together: 'You feel worried. I'm right here, and we'll go one step at a time.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the check-up
goals: Play doctor at home with a toy, then switch roles
Practise breathing for the stethoscope and saying aah
Say the steps once more and end with going home
rehearsal.parentSkill: Let your child be the doctor first and check you, then check a toy, then switch.

steps: Say hello at the front desk and wait in the waiting room
A nurse calls our name and walks us to a room
Stand on the scale and stand tall to measure height
Sit on the exam table with the crinkly paper
The doctor listens to the heart and tummy with a stethoscope
The doctor looks in the ears, eyes and mouth with a little light
sensory: a cold stethoscope on the chest
crinkly paper on the exam table
a small bright light for ears and eyes
a flat stick that touches the tongue
a blood pressure cuff that squeezes the arm, then lets go
a clean smell like hand soap
a waiting room with toys and other families
honestyNotes: A check-up is mostly looking and listening. Some parts feel strange: a cold stethoscope, a cuff that squeezes, a stick on the tongue. Some check-ups include a shot; if you know there will be one, say so honestly and use the shot story as well. Never promise there will be no shot unless you are sure.

fallbackAnswer: Most check-ups are just looking and listening.
Sometimes there is a shot too, and [[GROWNUP]] will tell you before the visit if there is one.

questionButtons.text: Why do I go if I am not sick?
fallbackAnswer: A check-up is how the doctor sees that your body is growing strong.
Healthy kids go to the doctor too, about once a year.

questionButtons.text: What is that thing on the doctor's neck?
fallbackAnswer: It is a stethoscope. It lets the doctor hear your heart go thump-thump.
It can feel cold, and you can ask to listen to your own heart.
Yes. [[GROWNUP]] stays in the room the whole time.
You can hold a hand or sit on a lap for some parts.
A nurse and a doctor. Their job is to help kids stay healthy.
They will tell you what they are going to do before they do it.

questionButtons.text: Do I take my clothes off?
fallbackAnswer: Sometimes the doctor asks to take off a shirt or shoes to listen and look.
Only the doctor or nurse checks, with [[GROWNUP]] right there, and you can always ask why.

questionButtons.text: What is the squeezy thing on my arm?
fallbackAnswer: It is a cuff. It gives your arm a tight hug for a few seconds.
Then it lets go with a little whoosh.
After the check-up we say goodbye and go home.
Maybe we can read a book or play together.

techniques.label: Holding a hand
techniques.how: Stand or sit where your child can hold your hand during each part of the exam.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Sitting on a grown-up's lap
techniques.how: Ask if your child can sit on your lap for the ears, eyes and mouth check.

techniques.label: Listening to my own heart
techniques.how: Ask the doctor to let your child listen to their own heart or to yours with the stethoscope first.

techniques.label: Playing doctor at home
techniques.how: Use a toy doctor kit or a paper tube to check a toy, then let your child check you.

techniques.label: Bringing a comfort toy
techniques.how: Let your child bring a favourite toy; the doctor can check the toy first.

techniques.label: Asking 'what's next?'
techniques.how: Teach your child to ask 'what's next?' and ask the doctor to name each step before it happens.

techniques.label: Counting to ten
techniques.how: Count slowly to ten together during each short part; most parts end before ten.

techniques.label: A sticker or a treat after
techniques.how: Plan a small reward or a favourite activity for after the visit and talk about it in the waiting room.

ritual: Breathe in, breathe out for the doctor

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] will go to the doctor for a check-up.
A check-up is how the doctor sees that a body is growing well.
First, [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] say hello at the front desk.
Then they wait in the waiting room, where there are books and toys.
Next, a nurse calls [[CHILD]]'s name.
Before bed, [[GROWNUP]] tells [[CHILD]] an old story about three little pigs.
The three little pigs each built a house.
One house was made of straw, and one house was made of sticks.
The third house was made of strong red bricks.
Every year, a kind old builder came to visit the brick house.
The builder did not come to fix anything.
The builder came to look and listen, to see that the house was strong.
First, the builder said hello at the gate.
Then the builder walked all around the house, step by step.
A check-up at the doctor is a bit like that.
The doctor looks and listens, to see that a body is strong and growing.
Tomorrow evening, the story goes on.
After that, [[CHILD]] stands tall on a scale and against a measuring line.
Then [[CHILD]] sits on a table with crinkly paper on top.
The doctor listens to [[CHILD]]'s heart and tummy and looks in the ears, eyes and mouth.
Last of all, everyone says goodbye, and [[CHILD]] goes home.
At the doctor, the steps go in order.
First, the waiting room, with books, toys and other families.
Then a nurse calls [[CHILD]]'s name and walks with [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] to a room.
Next, the scale and the measuring line, to see how much [[CHILD]] has grown.
After that, the table with the crinkly paper.
The doctor listens to the heart with a stethoscope, which may feel cold.
The doctor looks in the ears and eyes with a small bright light.
The doctor may touch the tongue with a flat stick and ask for a big aah.
Last, everyone says goodbye.
When the steps are known, the visit feels less new.
At the doctor's office there are a few helpers.
A friendly person at the front desk says hello and writes down [[CHILD]]'s name.

In the old story, the little pig felt shy when the builder came.
The builder had a big coat and a bag of tools.
So the builder said a friendly hello and told the pig about the job.
My job is to check that your house is strong, said the builder.
I will knock on the walls and listen.
I will look through the windows and up the chimney.
The little pig watched from the doorway.
Soon the little pig was not shy at all.
The pig even helped carry the tool bag.

The doctor and the nurse have jobs too.
Their job is to help children stay healthy and strong.
The doctor checks lots of kids every day.

A yearly check-up is the doctor's way of seeing how [[CHILD]] is growing.
First comes check-in, then a nurse measures height and weight and may take blood pressure with a cuff that squeezes the arm for a moment.
In the exam room, the doctor listens to the heart and lungs, looks in the ears and throat, and presses gently on the tummy.
They also ask questions about sleep, food and school.

The doctor comes next and does the main exam.
